packageRules.description: Reimplements group:allNonMajor plus digest updates, since the preset's minor/patch match misses digests

The node pins track the latest major, not LTS, so a node major merges itself once green. CI runs on the mise pin; release.yml's setup-node pin (packageName actions/node-versions) only runs at release. Ordered after the major rule, since later packageRules win.
A minor bump on a 0.x cargo dep is a breaking change under semver, so it gets its own PR and a human reviewer. Must stay ordered after the grouping rule above, since later packageRules win.

ADR-0025 keeps this pin, Cargo.toml's rust-version, and rust-toolchain.toml's channel equal, so bumping it raises the version oakum supports. That is a distribution decision and gets a human, in ONE grouped PR across all three files — the layout test fails any PR that moves fewer. The mise and rust-toolchain managers both emit a bare 'rust' depName (verified against Renovate 44.48.3 source); the regex manager below covers rust-version, which no native manager reads.

The install-action pin is printed output under crates/oakum. Renovate's chore(deps) commit releases nothing, so `check --strict` passes without a bump file and the printed workflow would ship only with the next release; a human decides whether it releases now. It gets its own PR; ordered after the grouping rule, since later packageRules win.
prBodyNotes: This pin is part of the workflow `oakum init` and `oakum migrate` print. The PR passes `check --strict` as is and releases nothing; to release the new pin, add a bump file: `mise run oakum -- add --packages "oakum:<level>" --message "..."`, with the level from the table in docs/contributing/task-tracking.md.

packageRules.description: serde-saphyr decodes pnpm catalogs, and its minor releases have changed what they read (1.3 decoded an empty block scalar as "" instead of null, okm-ab1n), so any update Renovate proposes for it gets its own PR and a human rather than riding the group; ordered after the grouping rule, since later packageRules win.
A cargo-dist bump needs release.yml regenerated by hand, so it gets its own PR and a human; ordered after the grouping rule, since later packageRules win.

customManagers.description: Cargo.toml's rust-version is the pin's third copy; Renovate's cargo manager does not read it (docs/research/renovate-rule-matching.md).

The install-action pin in the workflow oakum prints for a Cargo repository is a Rust constant, which no native manager reads (okm-oapg.1). It is a commit and its tag, read the way the dist-workspace.toml manager reads its action pins, so a bump moves both.

cargo-dist writes release.yml's action SHAs from [dist.github-action-commits], so the pin there is the source; Renovate's toml handling does not read it. depType action puts these under helpers:pinGitHubActionDigestsToSemver, so they resolve to the same exact versions as release.yml's pins; sharing a depName, both are expected in one PR.
The cargo-dist version release.yml was generated with. A bump means regenerating release.yml by hand (dist-workspace.toml's allow-dirty comment), so it never automerges.
